exam.title: MIT 6.0001: Functions, Data Structures & Recursion
exam.description: College exam testing function abstraction, list mutability and aliasing, dictionary lookups, and recursive divide-and-conquer.
exam.instructions: Answer all questions rigorously showing all work where applicable. Time limit: 60 minutes.

questions.text:
Consider the following code snippet:
```python
a = [1, 2, 3]
b = a
b.append(4)
print(len(a))
```
What is printed?
questions.rubric: Variable assignment `b = a` binds b to the same list object in memory (aliasing). Mutating `b` mutates `a`, so `len(a)` is 4.

questions.text: Which of the following data types CANNOT be used as a key in a Python dictionary?
questions.rubric: Dictionary keys must be hashable and immutable. Lists are mutable and do not implement __hash__, raising TypeError: unhashable type: 'list'.

questions.text: Write a recursive Python function `fib(n)` with a memoization dictionary that computes the n-th Fibonacci number in O(n) time instead of exponential O(2^n) time.
questions.correct_answer: def fib(n, memo={0: 0, 1: 1}): if n not in memo: memo[n] = fib(n-1, memo) + fib(n-2, memo); return memo[n]
questions.rubric: Full marks for providing a base case, recursive step, and storing previously computed values in a dictionary to prevent redundant subproblem calls.
